title: Async/Await Basics
summary: Understand how async/await simplifies asynchronous code.

scenes.narration: Welcome to our lesson on async/await. Let's dive into how it simplifies asynchronous code.
scenes.heading: Async/Await Basics

scenes.narration: Here we define an asynchronous function named fetchData.
This line logs 'Fetching data...' to the console.
We use the await keyword here to wait for the simulateFetch function to complete.
Once simulateFetch is done, we log its result to the console.
Now, let's look at the simulateFetch function. It returns a promise.
Inside the promise, we use setTimeout to simulate a delay of 2000 milliseconds, or 2 seconds.
So when we run it, 'Fetching data...' prints right away, then after 2 seconds, 'Data fetched!' appears.
Let's recap. Async functions make asynchronous code easier to read and write. Await pauses the function until the promise resolves. SimulateFetch mimics data fetching with a delay.
points: Async functions allow us to write asynchronous code that looks synchronous.
The await keyword pauses the execution of the async function until the promise is resolved.
simulateFetch simulates fetching data with a delay using a promise and setTimeout.
